business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) and Digital Scanning

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system, with commercial courts and dual public/private law; company law codified in the French Commercial Code)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Agreement for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 2007, entered into force 2010)
France-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1994, as amended by protocol)
France-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (applicable to frontier/cross-border structures in EU)
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force 1 February 2019)
EU-South Korea Free Trade Agreement (in force July 2011)
France has an extensive network of 100+ active bilateral investment treaties and 170+ tax treaties covering most non-resident shareholder jurisdictions.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L561-1 to L561-50 and R561-1 et seq., as transposed from Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Décret n° 2018-330 du 3 mai 2018 and the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles R123-210 to R123-222 establish the beneficial-owner (bénéficiaire effectif) declaration required for every legal entity registered at the Registre national des entreprises (RNE). The national financial intelligence unit TRACFIN and the ACPR supervise AML/CFT obligations. Failure to file true UBO information carries administrative fines and imprisonment for false declarations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid national identity document for each natural-person UBO and each proposed gérant (manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identity/immigration authority or notary in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate extract of any non-French corporate shareholder, including ultimate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record clearance for the proposed gérant (French bulletin n°3 or equivalent foreign judicial clearance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National judicial or criminal records authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of the gérant and UBOs (utility or bank statement, less than 90 days old)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (if not a Hague apostille country; EU documents may be accepted under existing judicial cooperation rules)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all non-French-language UBO and incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator registered with a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: None if translator is sworn; the underlying document must remain apostilled/legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney where incorporation is conducted by an agent on behalf of a non-resident founder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, shareholders, proposed gérants and beneficial controllers against: (i) the European Union's consolidated financial sanctions list; (ii) the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists; (iii) France's national asset-freezing and solicitation-notice files maintained by TRACFIN; (iv) OFAC's SDN and 13662 lists where USD transactions or US correspondents are planned; and (v) national criminal record and administrative disqualification lists. PEP status is determined by direct sworn confirmation plus a commercial database check; enhanced due diligence (EDD) and senior management approval are required for any PEP, high-risk-country, or opaque-nominee fact pattern. The SARL itself, if acting as a domiciliation/CMRA service provider, must register its own AML programme, appoint a compliance officer and file suspicious activity reports (déclaration de soupçon) with TRACFIN.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with the public searchable history in the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) at data.inpi.fr and Infogreffe.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registration documents and the statuts must be drafted in French; the corporate name may include foreign terms in Latin script, but any non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters and, where necessary, accompanied by a certified French translation. The chosen name must not be contrary to public order, must not mislead as to the legal form or regulated activity, and must comply with the Loi Toubon (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994) for all documents addressed to the public. A separate commercial sign (enseigne) may be used, but it does not create any name clearance at the RNE.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: SARL / SA / SAS / SCA / SNC (only permitted where the company actually uses exactly that legal form)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — French national tax authority; professional tax portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate formation and registration via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI; non-resident VAT direct registration desk: Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), 10 rue du Centre, 93166 Noisy-le-Grand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL with foreign shareholders: (1) execute the statuts, appoint a gérant, and block the share capital (minimum capital optional; commonly EUR 1–1,000); (2) file the incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, which broadcasts the file to the RCS/greffe, INSEE and DGFiP; (3) obtain the SIREN number (9 digits), SIRET (14 digits), extrait Kbis, and automatic ex officio VAT/corporate tax accounts; DGFiP assigns the intra-Community VAT identification number (format FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN), verifiable in VIES; (4) for a foreign entity without a French fixed establishment seeking direct French VAT registration, file an application with SIEE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères) together with foreign corporate registry extracts, identification forms, and supporting documents; SIEE issues the TVA intracommunautaire number normally within 2 to 4 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax — impôt sur les sociétés — at 25% headline rate, with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs); Territorial_Scope applies (French corporate tax is limited to profits attributable to French operations — principle of territoriality); Pass_Through_Eligible exists only under narrow statutory options (e.g., Art. 239 bis A/A bis CGI for family-controlled SARLs, or the option for partnership-style income tax treatment under Art. 239 bis AA CGI); no general Tax_Exempt_Zone applies to this business segment in metropolitan France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available elections: (1) option for income tax treatment for SARLs held by a handful of individual shareholders (Art. 239 bis AA and 239 bis A CGI), revocable for a renewable 5-year period; (2) election of the corporate income tax regime for otherwise transparent vehicles; (3) French fiscal consolidation (intégration fiscale, Art. 223 A CGI) for groups holding at least 95% of a subsidiary; (4) micro-BIC / simplified real regime options for small taxpayers; (5) anti-hybrid classification is governed by EU ATAD rules as transposed by the French Finance Acts, so structurally transparent foreign instruments may be recharacterized for French tax purposes; tax advice should confirm that the SARL is not treated as a disregarded entity in any counterpart jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Established SARL: no mandatory turnover threshold — VAT registration is required from the first taxable transaction unless the franchise en base de TVA (Art. 293 B CGI) applies; 2023/2024 franchise thresholds: EUR 91,900 for predominantly goods transactions and EUR 36,800 for services (mail scanning/virtual office services fall under the services threshold); non-established EU suppliers: EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance-selling threshold before French VAT registration (or OSS election); non-EU suppliers: zero threshold — mandatory direct registration (often with a VAT fiscal representative under Art. 289 A CGI) from the first taxable sale.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a full e-invoicing/e-reporting mandate (Loi de finances 2022, decree n° 2022-1299): from 1 September 2026 all VAT-registered businesses must be able to receive e-invoices and large/mid-size enterprises must issue structured e-invoices (Factur-X, UBL or CII) via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP); from 1 September 2027 all businesses (including micro-entities) must issue e-invoices; e-reporting will capture cross-border B2B/B2C data and domestic B2C payment data in parallel; no continuous-transaction-control digital stamping (e.g., Italy/Spain style) exists today, but cash registers and billing software for consumer cash transactions must satisfy Art. 286 CGI quater anti-fraud certification (NF 525); B2G invoicing uses Chorus Pro.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The virtual office / mail scanning activity is a B2B service. When supplied to a taxable business established outside France, the place of supply is the customer's establishment (Art. 259-1° CGI), placing the transaction outside the scope of French VAT (effective 0%); for intra-EU B2B supplies the customer applies reverse charge, and the French supplier must hold the customer's valid VAT number (VIES). Physical export of goods is zero-rated under Art. 262-I CGI only where a customs export declaration (DAU) and transport proof are retained. Caution: supplies to non-taxable private persons established outside the EU are not automatically out of scope; under Art. 259 B CGI they remain taxable in France unless a specific exception (not applicable to CMRA services) applies. Criteria to claim zero/out-of-scope treatment: contract naming the foreign customer, customer business registration/VAT evidence, performance evidence (scanning, mail forwarding logs), and bank-inward remittance proof.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU / déclaration en douane) evidenced through the DELTA system, where physical goods are exported
Commercial contract and VAT invoice with zero-rated/out-of-scope mention and cross-border B2B clause
Client VAT identification extract for EU taxables (VIES validation) or foreign trade registry extract for non-EU taxables
Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill for any physical dispatches of scanned mail or archives
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/bank statement evidencing payment from the foreign client account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP audit (vérification de comptabilité) places the burden of substantiation on the exporting supplier; failure to produce contemporaneous export/service evidence triggers reassessment of VAT at 20%, plus default interest (0.20% per month) and penalties of 40% (bad faith) or 80% (fraudulent maneuvers, Art. 1729 CGI), with a standard 3-year statute of limitations (Art. L169 LPF) extendable in hidden-activity or fraud scenarios; criminal tax fraud (Art. 1741 CGI) is punishable by up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment. Retroactive clawbacks will disallow previously zero-rated outputs and associated input VAT credits. France does not impose a statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, but the 180-day benchmark is retained here as prudent payment-trail discipline: delayed or unmatched inward remittances are a classic red flag for fictitious export claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with regulatory enforcement authority delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking and prudential supervision; foreign exchange and balance-of-payment reporting is administered jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor under EU capital movement liberalization rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a Eurozone member, maintains full capital and current account convertibility under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Article 63) and the EU Capital Movements Directive (Directive 88/361/EEC). No exchange control authorization is required for profit remittances, dividend distributions, loan repayments, or trade settlements involving EUR and other freely convertible currencies. However, statistical reporting obligations apply to cross-border flows exceeding EUR 12,500 per transaction under the French Foreign Exchange and Financial Relations Code. Profit remittance from a SARL is permitted upon satisfying corporate tax filing obligations and, for dividends, the approval of the shareholders' meeting; a tax clearance certificate is not statutorily required for dividend remittance but may be requested by the paying bank to meet compliance due diligence. Non-EUR transactions are subject to market pricing; no central bank intervention or specific conversion quota applies. Capital account operations such as direct investment, real estate acquisitions, and intellectual property transfers are freely liberalized, subject only to post-event reporting and anti-money laundering checks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement in France to repatriate or surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France. Exporters are free to hold foreign currency receipts in domestic or foreign bank accounts, provided such accounts are declared to the tax authorities and the cross-border movement of funds is reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistical purposes when the individual payment exceeds EUR 12,500. No mandatory conversion ratio applies; companies may retain EUR or convert to foreign currency as commercial prudence dictates. For invoicing in EUR, the settlement is cleared through TARGET2 or correspondent banking. Exporters of goods and services must maintain documentary evidence of the underlying commercial transaction for a period of at least six years to satisfy customs, tax, and AML verification requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB (Corporate and Investment Banking)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) authorized under the ACPR passporting regime, such as Qonto, Shine, and Lydia, are viable for a SARL's operational banking needs, particularly for virtual office and mail scanning services where low-cost account management and online settlement are desirable. Non-EU offshore digital EMIs without an ACPR license or an EU/EEA passport are not viable for holding client funds or conducting regulated payment services in France; they may only serve as auxiliary software/platform providers without engaging in money transmission. A French SARL must maintain its primary operational bank account with a licensed credit institution or an ACPR-registered EMI. Onboarding viability with EMIs is rated High for day-to-day treasury activity, but the Capital Escrow Account must be opened with a fully regulated bank to ensure credibility with creditors and to avoid liquidity risk. EMIs are subject to safeguarding requirements, and their cross-border clearing is limited to electronic money and payment initiation services; they do not provide commercial lending or trade finance instruments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SARL, the legal representative (gérant) must be physically present or remotely authenticated through a bank-accepted secure video identification process, provided the bank's internal policies allow remote onboarding. In practice, most tier-1 French banks require at least one physical meeting for the final sign-off of the corporate mandate, especially when the SARL has non-resident shareholders or operates in a higher-risk business classification. Remote opening is increasingly accepted for fintech EMIs using ACPR-compliant digital identity verification, but the opening of a traditional commercial bank account and, critically, the Capital Escrow Account, usually mandates physical attendance of the gérant or a duly appointed representative with a certified notarized power of attorney. Banks will verify the identity of all beneficial owners owning more than 25% of the SARL; these individuals may be required to appear or submit biometric identification processed via an ACPR-approved digital ID provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: Nominee shareholders, complex multi-jurisdictional ownership chains, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) under French AML law (Monetary and Financial Code Article L561-2-2).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized and apostilled register of actual shareholders, a full organizational chart tracing funds and control through each layer, copies of passport/ID of all UBOs, a declaration from each UBO confirming no criminal record for financial offenses, and a legal opinion from a French avocat confirming the SARL's ownership structure is not designed to evade transparency. The SARL's Articles of Association must be annotated to identify individuals holding more than 25%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-model red flags: Virtual office / mail scanning classified as 'commercial mail receiving agency' may be perceived as a conduit for shell companies, money laundering, or invoice fraud, given the medium-risk enhanced AML classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a detailed commercial contract with each client, proof of a physical service location (leased office or genuine business center), sample of standardized mail handling and scanning procedures, a privacy policy aligned with GDPR, identification of all client companies via KYC checks, prohibition of use for nominee/bank account opening, and a client acceptance policy that rejects high-risk industries. Maintain an audit trail of all mail, package logs, and scanned documents with timestamps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds ambiguity: Large or sudden capital injections from non-EU jurisdictions, especially in jurisdictions considered high-risk by FATF.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide source-of-wealth statements, bank statements for at least the past 12 months of the contributing entity, tax returns of the contributing entity, signed shareholder loan agreements with repayment terms, proof of registration and economic substance of the parent company, and a breakdown of the funds' origin. If funds derive from trading operations, provide underlying invoices and customs declarations; if from employment or sale of assets, provide pay slips or notarized sale contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction purpose misalignment: The declared activity being 'mail scanning' is not conclusively linked to the planned wire transfers or high-volume receipts from foreign clients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present contracts with service recipients, a service-level agreement (SLA) specifying the volume of mail and digital scans, a tariff list for each service, expected monthly recurring revenue, an operational budget projecting cash flows, and a business plan demonstrating that the bank account activity will be commensurate with the declared commercial purpose. Provide client diversity to avoid concentration risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax or corporate compliance sanctions: Failure to register the SARL's beneficial owners with the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs or pending tax disqualifications.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce the official registration confirmation from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), the 'extrait Kbis' dated within three months, the current UBO declaration receipt, and a tax compliance certificate issued by the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques confirming no outstanding corporate tax arrears or fraudulent activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the French SARL's corporate account must be initiated via SWIFT wire transfers using the SARL's IBAN (FR76 format) and BIC code. The transfer must include a proper purpose code in accordance with Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting. For direct investment equity contributions, use purpose code 'F1010' (capital share subscription) or 'F1020' (additional paid-in capital); for shareholder loans, use 'S3010' (commercial credits, advances and deposits) or the relevant code for financial operations. The sending bank must receive a copy of the notarized share subscription agreement, corporate resolution, or shareholder loan agreement to release the funds. Inbound transfers must state the economic nature in the 'remittance information' field, such as 'capital increase FR_SARL' or 'shareholder loan'. The receiving French bank will verify the beneficial owner details and may request a certificate of tax residence from the remitting entity to ensure compliance with the EU Anti-Money Laundering Directive and the French Monetary and Financial Code. If the transfer exceeds EUR 12,500, the SARL must report the transaction to the Banque de France within 10 business days using the standard CERFA form or via the online portal.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements must be executed through SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for direct payments to suppliers, or through a commercial letter of credit (documentary collection) issued by the French bank under ICC UCP600 rules for goods transactions. The SARL's virtual office business, being service-oriented, will primarily utilize MT103 transfers for recurring fees, subcontractor payments, and profit distributions. Each outbound payment must include the correct purpose code and be accompanied, when required, by underlying invoices or contracts. For payments to countries with exchange controls, the French bank will require a compliance review of the transaction against EU sanctions and embargo lists. Commercial letters of credit are permissible for trade settlement of physical goods if the SARL expands into billing and forwarding operations; in that case, the account must be designated as 'trade account' and the bank will issue the LC based on an underlying sale contract and proforma invoice. The recommended clearing rail is TARGET2 for EUR-denominated settlements, SWIFT for cross-currency, and SEPA instant credit transfers within France for domestic sub-5-second payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/non-EUR forwards (under ISDA 2002 or French FBF master agreement)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to restricted convertibility, accepted by French banks when the underlying trade or investment is genuinely risked and not speculative
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term shareholder loans or capital structures with non-EUR debt
FX options (European-style) for asymmetric hedging of receivable/payable exposure
Currency swaps executed on-exchange or via a regulated ACPR-licensed investment firm under EU EMIR reporting obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual situation confirmation (confirmation d'examen de situation) certifying no unresolved changes to registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Greffe du tribunal de commerce / Guichet des formalités des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after each anniversary of the company's RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry warning and formal notice; continued non-filing may cause the public prosecutor to request court-ordered strike-off (radiation) of the company from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) comprising balance sheet, income statement and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the close of each fiscal year and after approval by the ordinary shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to €9,000 against the legal representative; court injunction to compel filing; repeated failure can lead to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary annual shareholders' meeting (AGO) approving the annual accounts and allocation of results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; minutes recorded in the corporate minute book and referenced in the RCS accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the close of each fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Legal representative exposed to a fine up to €1,500; non-approval of accounts triggers procedural irregularity and may support claims for judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration / annual UBO confirmation (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) and updates on share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation submitted with the anniversary declaration; any change in UBO identity or holding percentage filed within 30 days of the relevant share transfer or change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to €15,000 for the legal entity and up to €7,500 for the legal representative; plus registry penalties and potential temporary restriction on filing other RCS acts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at the close of a fiscal year, it exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds: balance sheet total above €4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT above €8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Minority shareholders holding at least 10% of capital may also request a court-appointed auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the EU is mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups. Individual statutory accounts of a private SARL are prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, PCG), complying with the French Commercial Code faithful image principle.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code, every registered legal entity must file its beneficial owner list at incorporation and update the RCS within 30 days of any change affecting the identity or percentage of beneficial owners. The annual situation confirmation due in the anniversary month serves as the annual attestation that UBO information is still accurate; any share transfer resulting in a change of control or the crossing of the 25% holding threshold must be declared to the RCS within the same 30-day period.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / share transfer register (registre des associés / mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors and Manager decisions (registre des décisions de direction)
Minute Book of shareholders' meetings (registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 - $900 per year for a French domiciliation / virtual office and mail scanning service, depending on city and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500 - $9,000 per year for a certified audit engagement of a small-to-medium SARL, if the statutory audit thresholds are exceeded

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate; reduced 15% on first €42,500 taxable income for qualifying SMEs)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CIR tax credit for R&D, CII innovation tax credit, family/job protection? etc.
